+  M O R E   M A I L ! ! +

  September, 1991    Page Reply

 Alan Cox.............02    06

 Malcolm Perry........09    24

 Peter Quanstrom......26    28

 Simon Greenfield.....30    38

 George Robson........41    45

From Alan D. Cox, ST. CLEARS

Dear Brian,

I recently wanted to print SAM
keywords from BASIC,as one could
with the Spectrum using CHR$ n,
but SAM insists on printing the
corresponding UDGs, etc. I
remembered your CODELISTA in
Issue 33 so I thought that would
tell me how. You cheated! - You
did it all with DATA statements!

I have all the back SAM-related
issues of OUTLET but I have not
yet read them all so I do not
know if you have done anything
in this area since 33. In case
not, as I have (near enough)
solved the problem, I am sending
you this short note.

With ROM1 paged in at &F000 by
POKEing bit 6 of the LMPR to
unity, the keyword table is at
&F8C8 and it can readily be
printed out with RST 10.


To get specific messages, JPOMSG
at &0115 works like PO-MSG in
the Spectrum, with A selecting
the correct message from a table
stored at DE.


A suitable program - not too
naive, I hope: I claim no great
skill with machine code - which
nearly always works is...

IN A,&FA     Read LMPR
PUSH AF      Save copy
OR &40       Set bit 6
LD C,A       Put it in C

LD A,&AF     LMPR address to A
OUT (C),A    Put ROM1 at &F000
LD DE,&F8C8  Table address in DE
LD A,00      Poke 00 with entry
             No. before calling
             this program

CD &0115     Call "PO-MSG" to
             print keyword

POP AF       Recover orig. LMPR
LD C,A       Put it in C
LD A,&FA     LMPR address in A
OUT (C),A    restore orig. LMPR
RET

I am still finding what I regard
as bugs in the latest ROM but
one of the most irritating ones
is what I call the "reverse
listing" bug. I am not sure if
you have experienced this but if
I have a long program and want
to look at a line whose position
I only roughly remember then I
sometimes LIST at a line later
than I want. If I then stop
scrolling and try to go back up
the listing with the up arrow
sometimes(ALWAYS if I am due for
back-up!) I get a system reset.
I have called the author(s) of
the ROM many unrepeatable names
when this happens.
                Best wishes,

                Alan D. Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

I'm not sure about this reverse
listing bug. The most common bug
that annoys me is when BASIC is
still there but it will not take
any further commands without the
keyboard locking up.One can exit
from that by pressing the BREAK
button button but you can't even
SAVE the program and reload it!
The only thing you can do is to
cursor up and down the listing.
Entering: LIST just locks up but
pressing RETURN gives an auto
LIST.I probably have come across
the bug you describe but perhaps
didn't associate it with cursor
up - like you,I was probably too
busy muttering unrepeatable
names under my breath!

Many's the time I've sat, dazed,
staring at the pretty colours
after a reset crash - sort of
hypnotic - especially after an
hour's work is lost in eternity.

I get a similar feeling of shock
when the drive goes "chug, chug"
"Format data lost, Track 0,
Sector 1" and you try to absorb
the concept of the entire OUTLET
master being swallowed into the
abyss.

You've heard of shell shock.This
may be called"RESET SHOCK"and is
symptomised by the mind trying
to accept the unacceptable and
resisting the unbelievable. Ho,
hum - I must stop this. You just
caught me at a bad moment.

Oh, yes, about CODELISTA - the
DATA statements were only half
cheating - I didn't type them in
but used a little routine to
create a line using KEY IN with
the keyword, LIST it at the top
of the screen, then use SCREEN$
to convert the keyword into a
string and finally KEY IN to put
it in a DATA statement. In a FOR
NEXT loop it only took a few
minutes for the DATA to create
itself.Mind you,it took me about
16 hours to write the routine.

Thanks for the code routine any-
way. That's just the sort of
thing I like to have in OUTLET.

                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Perry,
      KIDDERMINSTER

I had started putting together a
controversial letter on: was Sam
being exploited to its best
advantage or were efforts being
'wasted'in the wrong directions?

However, a recent letter put the
same point across but I thought
I would add my thoughts in any
case. I hope I do not have to do
a S. Rushti (is that how you
spell it?) and go into hiding.

Please note this is intended as
an overall impression.It's in no
way written with any particular
item or source in mind or
intended.

As they say, any similarity
etc., is purely coincidental.
You are thinking of buying a
computer and go for a few
demonstrations. The DEMO usually
consists of routines or screens
to demonstrate its advertised
capabilities, e.g., if it has
fast data handling then this is
shown; same for high definition
screen, sound capabilities,
graphics and so on.


The demo usually demonstrates
these as separate items and if
you are lucky you get two or
more combined but that is
usually left to actual programs,
mainly games, to combine
multiple functions.

So having got your computer you
look around for software and
find plenty of different sources
and start collecting a few.
After running a number you (I)
begin to wonder: is this what I
bought the computer for?

The discs are, in content, to
greater or lesser extent the
same as the demo disc in the
shop I was looking at. When do I
get to "computing"?

Now a simple animation or what-
ever written in BASIC is far
more "useful" than say a multi-
coloured screen that is no more
than just a "screen picture" at
least the BASIC can be pulled
apart to learn about writing
BASIC routines.

(That is if it is not protected
to prevent you doing so, in that
case it is as useless as the
"screen picture").

Yes, the high definition digit-
ised screens are superb. The
originator has undoubtedly been
involved in a lot of work to get
them into their present shape
but what is the end result for
the user? I ask myself: "Did I
spend `300 to look at still
pictures of Blackpool Tower? A
picture postcard would only cost
a few pence and would show
better detail. So what next?
There's the sound - now again,
sound capabilities are superb.
Again it takes a lot of work and
skill to produce the sound
sequences and music passages.

I think if I wanted to listen to
music I have a record player
that plays music just as well if
not better. To make matters more
thought provoking, sound is
often with an almost blank still
screen or digitised screens
displayed in silence.

Digitised "recording" of sound
is another thought. A cynical
view could be that a tape-
recorder will record sound far
better and cheaper than a
computer. Apart from a novelty
value as a stand alone sequence
is it really any more than a
demo? Can playing through a
computer a digitised recording
of Maddona (or whoever) in any
way be considered as computing?

A workmate of mine once said
about something I told him I
could do with my computer: "but
what practical use is it?" and
that hit the nail on the head.
Apart from the demo of that
facility it had no practical use
whatsoever.

After you have looked at your
99th digitised screen you know
full well that it gives high
definition but things begin to
get boring.Two seconds of multi-
channel digitised Mozart is not
really a lot of use. I remember
that I bought a speech unit for
the Spectrum and a couple of
"talking" games. However, after
it had said for the 1000th time
in the same tone of 'voice'

"I'll get you Jetman" it was
more than grating on the nerves.
In fact the speech unit spent
most of its time in the drawer.

Now I do not say my views are
the majority and from the sales
figures of types of software
indicated I am certainly in the
minority. I would agree whole-
heartedly with any form of soft-
ware that generated interest and
promoted expansion of SAM.

Any user is certainly at liberty
to use the computer for whatever
purpose their interests lie and
as long as a certain type of
software is selling it will be
produced but what happens in the
future?

I wonder to what length of time
digitised screens will hold
interest once the initial
novelty value wears off? Will
the user still be overawed by
the umpteenth thousand 3 second
or so digitised music extract?


Without doubt in time all the
outstanding facilities will be
combined in a "useful" way
rather than simply as "demo.s"
Obviously now digitised screens
could be used in the same way as
clip art, music incorporated in
other routines but, as with the
'Jetman' example, if repeated
over and over again it can
become an annoyance rather than
an enhancement.

Games are no doubt the software
that makes or breaks a "domestic
market" type computer and it is
games where no doubt all the
outstanding functions within Sam
will be exploited.

'Outwrite!' is mentioned as an
example of putting efforts
towards a practical and useful
end result. Outlet, while it
contains items that I've been
"having a go" at contains a wide
mix and covers many interests
and it's a rare event if it does
not contain more than enough to
find of interest to offset items
that have no interest to me. I
ask,though,which would be likely
to hold interest longer, a
sequence of still frames in

silence followed by music
extracts to not too interesting
screens or a "demo" combining
two or more?

I concede the problem here is
that most of the items are
submitted by individuals. Some-
one who can produce screens
cannot produce music and an
expert on music sequences may
not be good at animation and so
on. Not an easy solution and any
combination would fall on those
assembling the disc.

Professional software houses are
a different kettle of fish. Yes,
there are quite a number of
utility routines appearing and
also games etc. and for Sam to


take its place in the market it
has to initially have a good
selling point and software to
satisfy and keep the user
interested, especially after the
initial novelty of demo type
software wears off.


I read a recent review that
ended by saying: "A well-
engineered solution to a non-
existent problem" and that is
what this is all about.

Is a lot of time and effort
being directed in the wrong
direction? Is time and effort
spent in producing no more than
"demo" type end results being
wasted or effectivly utilised?

I am no way putting down anyone
who has the ability to produce
such items but I do say once
something has been mastered the
art of digitising and then spend
all the time simply churning out
screens as if on a production
line or move on to and master
other aspects. Here I must admit
that I soon get bored with the
same old thing for too long and
chop and change interests nearly
as often as my socks.

On the subject of useful applic-
ations the household was shatt-
ered with a burst of laughter in
the early hours because I had
just read that a "velocity
sensitive " keyboard had been
developed for a certain make of
computer.

Having achieved this outstanding
accessory what mind-boggling use
had been found for it? - well,
it came with a software routine
so that if you hit the keys too
hard the computer said "OUCH"!
To be fair it was intended as an
aid to teach touch typists to be
light-fingered, oops, better
rephrase that! -to teach them to
be light on the keys.

I will end by saying that some
years ago, I considered the
various capabilities of the
Spectrum were put together into
an entertaining way that held
the user's interest without
becoming boring even though it
contained still "screens" short
passages of repeating "music"

and imaginative use of relative-
ly simple, at times, animation
but all-combined, the overall
effect was excellent."That's the
Ticket" was an ideal way to
relax after a frustrating time.

Before I end and wait for the
flak to descend, one final
question, why did not Sam at
least conduct in time with the
MGT Anthem on the demo?  A good
example where the animation
facility missed out, and yes it
could be done as I had him not
only conducting (with both hands
and arms) but also tapping his
foot! in time with the music.
Sorry no I do not have the copy
any more as the tape it was on
has been used for other things.

However, I consider it improved
the demo many hundred % (well I
would, wouldn't I, being the one
who did it?).

                 Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

This is a very advanced case of
reset shock I think caused by
not allowing the mind sufficient
time to adjust after a bad crash
on the computer.The symptoms are
classic:pondering the meaning of
life,the universe and everything
and can anything be worthwhile
unless it is "useful"?

Well, we all know what you mean
but really, I don't get bored
looking at demos and screens. I
don't anticipate a very lengthy
attention-span but then I don't
expect to pay `14.99 either.It's
like looking at a cartoon in the
newspaper: smile - then move on
to the next item.

(To the tune of "I Enjoy being a
Girl")...
I like computing. I like machine
code and BASIC. I like both to
program and to study others
programs. I like screens and
demos and games and sounds and
music and I never get tired of
the little digitized SCREAM in
PIPPO when you fall off the edge
and I like reading about
computers and computing and just
about every aspect of the whole
whacky world of this weird and
wonderful wonder machine. Except
bugs.And viruses.And crashes.And
when your tie gets caught in the
drive and you bang your chin on
the keyboard.And those horrible
85-column text screens in cyan
ink on magenta.And...
                        - Brian

From: Peter Quanstrom,EASTBOURNE

Thank you for your prompt reply
to my problem regarding printing
"Flash" with my Mannesmann MT-80
printer. Your advice, that the
letter from Colin Demaline
should be just what I need, was
correct and I was able to print
out Large & Small Dump together
with Large & Small Grey Dump
without any problem(Using solely
the para in Colin's letter
commencing "FLASH").

To print out your ADD-VERTS
page: this was achieved by going
to that page, keying in "ESC",
then "POKE SVAR 31,4: POKE SVAR
35,75"and after the message:"OK"
typing: GOTO 8000.

Lastly you requested the Tasword
2 Basic line 1470 which is:
CLS: GOSUB 1520: PRINT AT o,o,
"verifying";A$: VERIFY a$ CODE

In case I did not make myself
clear concerning the problem
message - "93 verify failed,
1470:4"; I wish to clarify that
Tasword 2 had been SAVEd on a
Master Dos formatted Disc and I
had transferred a Tasword 2 file
from a Sam Dos formatted disc.
(Should this have made any
difference ?).

Please extend my thanks to Colin
Demaline and to yourself, Brian,
for your most professional and
timely response which reflects
the quality of "Outlet".
              - Peter Quanstrom

Brian Cavers to Peter Quanstrom

Ah! - but you didn't reply to my
suggestion that you use SAMDOS
to see if that cures the bug. In
fact, it is not now clear to me
whether you were talking about
many (all) Tasword files failing
to verify or just one. If it is
just one file - could you reload
it later?

VERIFY will normally only fail
for two reasons. (1).The file is
corrupted on the disc and cannot
be reloaded. This will result in
a"Format" track and sector error
or similar. (2).The file in RAM
has been changed since the SAVE
and so does not match that on
the disc giving a "VERIFICATON
HAS FAILED" error.

It's theoretically possible that
a file might be corrupted on the
disc and thus not match that in
RAM giving a VERIFICATION error
but I believe all data SAVEd on
a disc is added up in a checksum
and any change would prevent re-
loading. It may also be that SAM
copies all data to a sector-size
buffer before saving and that
was corrupted just before saving
but I doubt this latter theory.

The reason I asked what was on
line 1520 was that any change
between a SAVE and a VERIFY may
affect the VERIFY. For example,
if you SAVE a BASIC program then
change a variable before VERIFY
it will fail or if you SAVE CODE
then POKE the code before VERIFY
it will fail.

From: Simon Greenfield, LINCS.


Dear Ron & Brian,

I've recently acquired my "so-
called" SAM-specific rodent from
SamCo and in all fairness have
to say I'm disappointed with the
way its turned out. I expected a
SAM mouse -one that was supposed
to do away with interfaces.
Instead we get an ST/AMIGA
switcheable mouse,the Contriver
and a not-so-small interface
that Alan Miles described in his
summer newsletter as being
"small". This interface is the
size of the "SDI" interface and
is identical to it as it's the
same shape and size casing.

After all this time SamCo could
have converted any mouse ages
ago instead of keeping us
waiting. I feel as though SamCo
are leading us up a rather long
garden path with all their hype!
Add to that the accompanying
software disk contained just
three programs for use with it -
a bug-riddled version of'FLASH',
a 'BASIC' routine, and a
'SLIDING TILE'game.Wow! Eighteen
months has achieved that. What
can you say? I'm gobsmacked. No
wonder they failed as MGT last
time.

There isn't even any accompany -
ing documentation except a
couple of rather pathetic
screens of text (even those are


not much cop!) for explaining
how to go about implementing the
mouse's X,Y commands - absolute
waste of time I think!!!!

I'll only keep my rodent due to
the fact that when SamCo said in
the summer newsletter that the
mouse was ready now when they
really meant they only actually
had 100 or so. The "first come
get first served" and that there
would be a delay waiting for
replacement stock to come in
from abroad. They asked for our
phone numbers on the order forms
so as to contact us in case of
difficulty or delay but chose to
do neither in reality (thanks
SamCo) I ended up waiting six
weeks without as much as a
"squeak!" from them.

Instead it was me who had to do
the phoning (good service eh??!)
and this will be the"main" mouse
for future software -plus there
is supposed to be a future
upgrade of the mouse version of
'FLASH'.

You may be interested to know
that my Genius mouse for my
Spectrum +3 actually works with
my SAM when attached to the SAM
mouse interface. The Contriver
mouse works vice-versa when
plugged into the interface on my
Spectrum +3. Therefore, why
could SamCo not offer us just
the interface as an alternative
to those with existing mice
instead of bundling the two
together, thereby saving time
and money!

SamCo fail to mention that the
Contriver mouse must be switched
to the ST position and also
previous existing versions of
'FLASH' DO NOT work. This was
stated to me by a SamCo rep over
the phone when I enquired as to
the whereabouts of my mouse!

Having whinged that off my chest
it is safe to say I have now all
but lost any faith in SamCo and
what they tell us from now on
concerning new products.

"How good is the SAM Mouse? The
best. We designed the central
chip in SAM - the BASIC - with
the Mouse in mind".

If so - why the interface?

I recently acquired the MIDI
sequencer from them for forty
quid. Although an extremely
powerful program which works
brilliantly, the fact that you
are not even permitted to backup
the disk for safety's sake and
peace of mind is, in my books,
ridiculous. When I queried this
with SamCo,apart from explaining
reasons of copyright (of which I
am fully aware) they said that
if your disk becomes corrupted
through normal use they or Mr.
Tim Humphries would replace it.
This is ridiculous as it would
probably take at least two weeks
for the turn around and wastes
postage and time. All for the
sake of being able to backup the
disk in the first place, logical
thinking I suppose??!!

Issue eleven of Sam Supplement
has a rather new snazzy look and
is advising readers to make sure
they obtain the next issue (12)
as it's their first birthday
issue. We are told it's going to
be rather special so all who are
still in doubt about Sam
Supplement and whether or not
it's worth it take it from me it
is. You won't be disappointed.

I have now dropped 'Format' as
it is not worth the effort
involved any more.

Readers of Sam Supplement who
subscribe here may or may not
have seen my letter in support
of Mr J.L. Phillips in Issue 8
of the Supplement describing my

little incident with the Editor
of Format - and indeed as in the
case of one reader who wrote in
complaining after he had only
read his first issue ie: "8" -
said I was abusing the user
group and the Editor with my
letter. Let me just say for the
record to any Format subscriber
who reads Outlet as well(or SS),
my letter was neither abusive
against Mr Brenchley nor the
user group. My comments were not
"erroneous" as Mr. Brenchley
replied to that reader in
question but were pure fact.

        Simon Greenfield..

Brian Cavers to Simon Greenfield

I've asked SAMCO for their comm-
ents on the points you raised
but have not heard from them yet
(at the time of writing).

I must admit I was disappointed
to hear that the interface was
not available separately from

It carried the same so-called

Sorry I had to cut many of your
comments about FORMAT but the
essence is there I think.

                       - Brian

Brian Cavers to George Robson

Thanks for the info, George. The

on SAM is HYDROFOOL. This runs
under EMUTILITY (OUTLET 34) with
no problems so I'm a little
surprised it doesn't work with
Lerm's SAMTAPE. I remember that
SWEEVO'S WORLD by the same soft-
ware house and using similar

                        - Brian.

From Alan D. Cox, ST. CLEARS

Dear Brian,

I recently wanted to print SAM keywords from BASIC,as one could with the Spectrum using CHR$ n, but SAM insists on printing the corresponding UDGs, etc. I remembered your CODELISTA in Issue 33 so I thought that would tell me how. You cheated! - You did it all with DATA statements!

I have all the back SAM-related issues of OUTLET but I have not yet read them all so I do not know if you have done anything in this area since 33. In case not, as I have (near enough) solved the problem, I am sending you this short note.

With ROM1 paged in at &F000 by POKEing bit 6 of the LMPR to unity, the keyword table is at &F8C8 and it can readily be printed out with RST 10.

To get specific messages, JPOMSG at &0115 works like PO-MSG in the Spectrum, with A selecting the correct message from a table stored at DE.

A suitable program - not too naive, I hope: I claim no great skill with machine code - which nearly always works is...

IN A,&FA     Read LMPR PUSH AF      Save copy OR &40       Set bit 6 LD C,A       Put it in C

LD A,&AF     LMPR address to A OUT (C),A    Put ROM1 at &F000 LD DE,&F8C8  Table address in DE LD A,00      Poke 00 with entry No. before calling this program

CD &0115     Call "PO-MSG" to print keyword

POP AF       Recover orig. LMPR LD C,A       Put it in C LD A,&FA     LMPR address in A OUT (C),A    restore orig. LMPR RET

I am still finding what I regard as bugs in the latest ROM but one of the most irritating ones is what I call the "reverse listing" bug. I am not sure if you have experienced this but if I have a long program and want to look at a line whose position I only roughly remember then I sometimes LIST at a line later than I want. If I then stop scrolling and try to go back up the listing with the up arrow sometimes(ALWAYS if I am due for back-up!) I get a system reset. VERIFY will normally only fail for two reasons. (1).The file is corrupted on the disc and cannot be reloaded. This will result in a"Format" track and sector error or similar. It may also be that SAM copies all data to a sector-size buffer before saving and that was corrupted just before saving but I doubt this latter theory.

The reason I asked what was on line 1520 was that any change between a SAVE and a VERIFY may affect the VERIFY. For example, if you SAVE a BASIC program then change a variable before VERIFY it will fail or if you SAVE CODE then POKE the code before VERIFY it will fail.

VERIFY обычно сбоит всего по двум причинам. (1). Файл на диске поврежден и не может быть прочитан заново. Это приведет к ошибке дорожки и сектора («Format») или аналогичной. (2). Также может быть, что SAM копирует все данные в буфер размером в сектор перед сохранением, и буфер был поврежден прямо перед записью, но в эту теорию верится с трудом.

Причина, по которой я спросил о строке 1520, заключалась в том, что любые изменения между SAVE и VERIFY могут повлиять на верификацию. Например, если вы делаете SAVE бейсик-программы, а затем меняете переменную перед VERIFY — произойдет сбой; или если сохраняете CODE, а затем меняете байт командой POKE в коде перед VERIFY — верификация также провалится.
